dedupe_keys.name: china ministry of emergency management typical cases of chemical and hazardous chemical production accidents 2021

description: This case study is the Chinese Ministry of Emergency Management's release of a batch of typical production safety accidents in chemical and hazardous chemical enterprises since 2021, published on 19 August 2021 to push local governments and companies to learn from them. It reports that China had 62 chemical accidents with 81 deaths in the first half of 2021, down from 80 accidents and 92 deaths a year earlier, but six larger accidents, three more than in the same periods of 2020 and 2019. Each case gives the date, company, casualties, direct economic loss, direct cause and main lessons, for example a nitrogen asphyxiation at a Henan plant that killed four, an explosion during illegal production in Hubei, and hydrogen sulphide poisonings in Jilin and Heilongjiang after ventilation lost power or gas was not purged. It is published by the ministry's News and Publicity Department. Coverage is national for China. The release is available free online as a web page in Chinese. Caveats: the cases are selected summaries, not full investigation reports, and no licence is stated. The ministry also warns that summer heat, lightning, heavy rain and wind raise the risk of overheating, fires and explosions at chemical sites. For simulation it supplies failure sequences for emergency response and resilience scenarios at chemical plants, including how a power cut to ventilation escalated into multiple deaths. It is related to the CSB recommendations database record in this catalogue, a US source of chemical incident lessons.
